findings.title: add_comment does not verify ticket existence
findings.explanation: The store's add_comment method inserts a comment row without checking that the referenced ticket_id exists. If called directly (bypassing TicketService), it can create orphan comments, violating data integrity.
findings.verification_note: The add_comment method in tickets/store.py inserts a comment without checking ticket existence, as shown by the code snippet lacking any verification.

findings.title: Rule: Public functions have type hints and a one-line docstring that says what they return or raise
findings.explanation: The public method `add_comment` has a type hint but its one-line docstring mentions only the raised exception and does not state what the function returns, violating the rule that docstrings must say what they return or raise.

evidence.quote: """Add a comment to an existing ticket. Raises ValueError if it is empty or longer than MAX_COMMENT."""

limitations: The review cannot determine if comment bodies are later rendered in a web context without proper escaping, which could lead to XSS vulnerabilities.

criteria.text: Any user can add a comment to an existing ticket.
criteria.explanation: The add_comment method accepts any author string and does not enforce permission checks, allowing any user to add a comment to an existing ticket.

criteria.text: An empty or whitespace-only comment is rejected.
criteria.explanation: add_comment strips whitespace and raises ValueError when the resulting body is empty, rejecting empty or whitespace‑only comments.

criteria.text: A comment is at most 2000 characters.
criteria.explanation: MAX_COMMENT is defined as 2000 and add_comment raises a ValueError if the comment length exceeds this limit, enforcing the "at most 2000 characters" rule.

evidence.quote:
if len(body) > MAX_COMMENT:

criteria.text: A ticket's comments are listed oldest first.
criteria.explanation: list_comments queries the comments table ordered by id, which reflects insertion order, and the test asserts that comments are returned oldest first.
